approach:
Leave `Athena::retry` and `Athena::ask` exactly as they are, because the automatic drain calls `retry` (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:4635) and about 70 tests call both. Add a guard for hand commands only, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, with three entry points that all call it: `retry_by_hand(job, force, ui)`, `ask_by_hand(text, force, ui)` and `queue_by_hand(text, force)`.

The guard refuses in two cases, and a refusal commits nothing:
- The named job has a retry that is Queued, Proposed, Blocked or Dispatched. A new helper finds it by scanning `job_history` for `retry_of == job`. The existing `retries_by_job` cannot be used: it keeps only the newest retry and counts closed ones.
- Athena's failure review of the job is pending. A new `failure_review_pending(records, job)` in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs says so when the job's state is Closed(Rejected or Failed) and it has no Rejection or Failure introspection record, other than a kill-switch-failed one. That is the same event set as `event_of_job` and `requeue_kill_switch_failures`.

With `--force` the guard lets the retry through. After the retry is queued it commits one `Intervention` record (category `OverrodeDecision`, source `Observed`). The interrupted-job refusal that `retry` already has is also bypassed when `--force` is given.

`--force` is added to `Command::Retry` and `Command::Ask` in main.rs. `athena status` gets a new `failure_note` field on `JobLine` and `JobTrace`, with its display. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry.

decisions.choice: Add new hand-only entry points (`retry_by_hand`, `ask_by_hand`, `queue_by_hand`) that run the guard and then call the unchanged `retry`, `ask` and `queue`. One private helper in reading.rs holds the guard.
decisions.reason: `Athena::retry` is also the automatic path: drain.rs:4635 (`ReadOf::Retry`) retries interrupted jobs through it. About 70 test call sites use it (crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs and others). The existing test `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice` (crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs:1282) calls it twice in a row. A guard inside `retry` would change automatic behaviour and break those tests. The guard still sits in one shared place in reading.rs, and every hand command calls it. Hand commands that queue a retry, re-ask or follow-up are `athena retry` and `athena ask` / `ask --later` with 'try again on <job>' text. `accept-proposal` (proposals.rs:643) and `approve-work` ask for new work, not a retry of a failed job. `correct` (reading.rs:1336) accepts only Proposed or Declined jobs.

rejected.option: Put the guard inside `Athena::retry` with a `force` parameter
rejected.why: It changes the automatic drain retry and breaks about 70 callers.

rejected.option: Copy the check into each command in commands.rs
rejected.why: Criterion 6 requires one shared path in reading.rs.

decisions.choice: A retry 'stands' (queued or running) when its state is Queued, Proposed, Blocked or Dispatched. Declined, Dropped, Abandoned, Stale, Closed and every ended state do not count. The helper scans `job_history(records)` for `retry_of == job`.
decisions.reason: `retry_follow_up` (retry.rs:277-283) already treats Queued, Proposed, Blocked and a Dispatched retry as 'run `athena go`' or 'wait'. `retries_by_job` (retry.rs:246) returns only the newest standing retry and counts a Failed or Landed retry, so a newer failed retry would hide an older queued one. A closed Failed retry is not queued or running, so retrying the job again stays allowed, as the brief says. The closing of a dropped retry is already covered by the existing test `a_dropped_retry_does_not_block_a_new_retry`.

rejected.why: It counts ended retries and keeps only the newest.

decisions.choice: `failure_review_pending` reads records only. It is true when job.state() is Closed(Rejected or Failed) and no introspection has job == the job, trigger Rejection or Failure, and (status Recorded, or status Failed with a failure that does not contain KILL_SWITCH_TEXT). A kill-switch-deferred review has no record, so it counts as pending.
decisions.reason: introspect.rs:1546-1550 shows only Rejected and Failed outcomes are events. run/mod.rs:431-437 runs the review right after `go`. A review that failed for another reason is final ('not queued again', introspect.rs:1495-1496), so it is not pending. A kill-switch failure is requeued (introspect.rs:1436-1492), so it is. The brief says 'pending when the job failed and its introspection record is not yet written'. Reading records avoids a filesystem read of `introspect_pending_dir`.

rejected.why: It would miss the short window between the outcome commit and the introspection commit.

decisions.choice: The forced override writes an `Intervention` with category `OverrodeDecision`, source `Observed`, job = the retried job, class_of_work = the job's class or 'unknown'. It is committed with `commit_records` after the retry is queued. If the commit fails, the error names the retry that was queued. No introspection is run for it.
decisions.reason: `OverrodeDecision` exists (athena-data records.rs:151). `InterventionSource::Observed` is documented as 'Captured by Athena itself' (records.rs:232), and `correct` already uses it (reading.rs:1395). `status::open_interventions` (status.rs:552-556) lists only `User` interventions as open work, so an Observed record adds no follow-up item. No athena-data change is needed, so crates/athena-data/src/records/core.rs and crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs stay untouched, although the brief lists them as expected deliverables. Recording after the retry means a refused or failed retry leaves no intervention. A model call per forced retry is avoided.

rejected.why: It would show as open work in `athena status` and would call the introspection model.
It would need an athena-data allow-list change for no gain.

rejected.option: Record before the retry is queued
rejected.why: A retry that fails afterwards would still leave an intervention.

decisions.choice: Status adds a new field `failure_note: Option<String>` to `JobLine` and `JobTrace`. It reads 'failure review pending', or 'retry <id> queued' / 'retry <id> running'. `JobLine.retried_as` (status.rs:100) is left alone.
decisions.reason: The doc of `retried_as` is 'The id of the retry that stands for this job, for an interrupted job that was already retried'. It feeds the interrupted next-line text (status.rs:1166) and display.rs:1078. Widening it would change those lines and counts closed retries. A new field avoids that. The note is computed by one pure function, `failure_note(records, job, running)`, so it can be tested without a repository. `athena status` reads records from the worktree (status.rs:1194-1195) while hand commands read HEAD; both are the same commit in normal use.

rejected.why: It would change its documented meaning and the interrupted next-line text.

decisions.choice: The hand guard is a new stage; every exit is tabulated in the reason.
decisions.reason:
(a) Refused for a standing retry: Err returned from `check_hand_retry` in reading.rs; message names the retry id, its state and the `retry_follow_up` text, and says 'Nothing was queued'. The CLI main prints it and exits non-zero. No commit, no job. The next reader of state is `athena status`, which still shows the job's failure_note.
(b) Refused for a pending review: same path and same state; the message says 'the failure review of job <id> is pending', and that `athena start` runs deferred reviews or `--force` queues a retry anyway.
(c) Forced past (a) or (b): the retry is queued through the unchanged `retry` or `ask`; then one Intervention is committed. Records afterwards: a new job and an intervention. Status counts it in `interventions_by_category`; scoring reads only the closed job's own interventions.
(d) Nothing blocks: the unchanged path runs and no intervention is written, whether or not `--force` is given.
(e) Error inside the guard (a record cannot be loaded): propagated with `?`, nothing committed.
(f) Hold, kill switch or line pause: the line-pause refusal (reading.rs:1280) and `refuse_if_stopped` (reading.rs:948) stay first and are unchanged.
(g) Interrupt: a process that dies between the retry commit and the intervention commit leaves a queued retry with no intervention. This cannot be made atomic without a combined commit, and the window is one commit; it is a stated limit.
(h) Preflight-stopped retry: the guard also checks the job `retry_target` resolves to (reading.rs:1304), so a duplicate of the original job is found too.

rejected.option: Commit the intervention in the same commit as the reading
rejected.why: `first_reading` builds that commit, and a guard there would also run for the automatic path.

files.purpose: Add `retry_by_hand`, `ask_by_hand`, `queue_by_hand` and the private shared `check_hand_retry` (standing-retry and pending-review refusals, force override, intervention commit). `retry` becomes a thin wrapper over a private inner function that holds the existing body and takes an optional hand argument. Its automatic behavior is unchanged.
Add `pub fn failure_review_pending(records, job) -> bool`, next to `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT` and `event_key`, which it reads.
Add `--force` to `Command::Retry` and `Command::Ask`, pass it through in `run`, update help text and the clap tests.
`retry` and `ask` take `force` and call `retry_by_hand`, `ask_by_hand` and `queue_by_hand`; print a note when a forced override was recorded.
Add `failure_note` to `JobLine` and `JobTrace`, the pure `failure_note` function, its fill-in in `scan_jobs` and `trace`, and unit tests.
Show the note in `plan_suffix` and in `trace`; add `failure_note: None` to the JobLine and JobTrace test fixtures.
New tests for the four acceptance cases, ask and queue, the binary refusal, help flags and status note; annotate `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice` as the automatic path.
Add a bullet under '## [Unreleased]' / '### Changed' (failure, fix, limits, tests).

steps: Read-only checks first, then edit in this order so the tree always builds.

Step 1 (introspect.rs): add `pub fn failure_review_pending(records: &Records, job: &JobRecords) -> bool` next to `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT` (line 820). It returns true when `job.state()` is Closed(Rejected or Failed) and no `records.introspections` entry has `job == job.id()`, trigger Rejection or Failure, and (status Recorded or a failure without KILL_SWITCH_TEXT). Re-export it through the crate paths that `introspect` items already use (check `lib.rs`).

Step 2 (reading.rs): add a private `live_retry_of(records, job_id) -> Option<(String, JobState)>` (scan `job_history(records)` for `retry_of == job_id` and a state of Queued, Proposed, Blocked or Dispatched). Add `struct HandOverride { job: JobId, what: String }` and `fn check_hand_retry(&self, records, job_id, force) -> Result<Option<HandOverride>>`: standing retry first, then pending review. It bails with the id/state/`retry_follow_up` text and 'Nothing was queued' when `force` is false, and returns the override when it is true. Then add `fn record_override(&self, ov, new_job)`, which commits an `Intervention` (category OverrodeDecision, source Observed, job = the retried job, class from `job.class()` else 'unknown', id checked with `records.has_record_id`) with `commit_records` and a `message(...)` as `correct` does (reading.rs:1371-1410, 1462). If the commit fails, add context naming the queued new job.

Step 3 (reading.rs): move the body of `retry` into `fn retry_inner(&self, job_ref, hand: Option<bool>, ui)`. `retry` calls it with `None`. `retry_by_hand(job_ref, force, ui)` calls it with `Some(force)` and then, when the guard returned an override, calls `record_override` after `ask` succeeds. In the body: after the line-pause check and `registry().reap()`, run `check_hand_retry` for the named job; after `retry_target`, run it for the target if it differs. The existing interrupted-job refusal (reading.rs:1288-1300) stays as is for `None` and for `Some(false)`. For `Some(true)` it is skipped and counted as an override. Add `ask_by_hand(text, force, ui)` and `queue_by_hand(text, force)`: load records at head, `retried_job(&records, text)`, run the guard, then call the unchanged `ask` / `queue` and record any override. Update the doc comment of `retry`.

Step 4 (main.rs and commands.rs): add `#[arg(long)] force: bool` with doc text to `Command::Retry` and `Command::Ask`. Update the dispatch at main.rs:1051-1057 and `commands::retry` / `commands::ask`, which call the hand methods and print one line when an override was recorded. Update the `retry` help text and add clap tests with `Cli::try_parse_from` for `retry <job> --force` and `ask --later --force`.

Step 5 (status.rs and display.rs): add `failure_note: Option<String>` to `JobLine` and `JobTrace` (skip when None). Add a pure `failure_note(records, job, running) -> Option<String>`: standing retry gives 'retry <id> queued' or 'retry <id> running', pending review gives 'failure review pending', in that order, only for Closed(Rejected, Failed, TimedOut or Stale) jobs. Fill it in `scan_jobs` and `trace`. Show it at the end of `plan_suffix` and as a line in `display::trace`. Fix the constructors at status.rs:911, display.rs:2679, :2770 and :2105. Add unit tests in status.rs.

Step 6 (tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs): add the tests named in the demonstrations (queued refusal with unchanged HEAD and job count, ask and queue refusals, pending refusal with the reset-to-before-the-review setup and the kill-switch and other-failure cases, no-block baseline, forced second retry with an intervention, force with nothing blocking writes none, Dispatched retry, preflight target, status note, help flags, binary refusal). Add a small `athena_bin(&fx)` helper copied from introspection.rs:292 for the binary test. Annotate `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice`.

Step 7 (CHANGELOG.md): add one bullet under '## [Unreleased]' / '### Changed' with the failure (a hand retry or re-ask of a failed job duplicating a retry that Athena already had queued or running, then closed as a duplicate, 2 jobs), the guard in reading.rs, `--force` and the intervention, the status note, what is unchanged (drain, steward), limits (jobs with no review record need `--force`; the intervention is committed after the retry), and the test commands.

Step 8: run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix any fixture constructors that miss the new field. Do not edit anything under records/, drain.rs or steward.rs.

risks.risk: An older failed or rejected job whose review was never written counts as pending forever and needs `--force` once.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text says how to proceed (`athena start` runs deferred reviews; `--force` queues a retry anyway). The change is stated in CHANGELOG.md limits. The brief defines pending as 'the job failed and its introspection record is not yet written', and this follows it.

risks.risk: Timed out or stale jobs, which `retry` accepts, are never reviewed, so a pending check on them would block them wrongly.
risks.mitigation: `failure_review_pending` returns false for every state except Closed(Rejected or Failed), the set `event_of_job` uses (introspect.rs:1546-1550). Timed out, stale and interrupted jobs are never pending, and the tests cover each state.

risks.risk: The refactor of `retry` into a wrapper changes the automatic path by mistake.
risks.mitigation: Entry points are new and `retry` and `ask` keep their signatures. The wrapper and the new method share one inner function, and the test suite (about 70 retry callers) is run in full.

risks.risk: The process dies between the retry commit and the intervention commit, leaving a forced retry with no intervention; or the intervention commit fails.
risks.mitigation: The error names the new job, so the owner can see it. It is a stated limit in CHANGELOG.md.

risks.risk: Status (worktree records) and a hand command (HEAD) disagree for a moment, so a note shows a retry the command no longer sees.
risks.mitigation: Prior retry of a retry chain: the guard checks both the named job and `retry_target`; a test covers a preflight-stopped retry. Status uses the same function with `running` from the registry.

risks.risk: The expected-deliverable list includes steward.rs and crates/athena-data/src/records/core.rs, which this plan does not edit.
risks.mitigation: Production code and tests stay in the files listed. `steward.rs` and athena-data `core.rs` are left untouched on purpose, since no change is needed there; the verifier checks the diff against the brief's criteria and not against that expected list.

demonstrations.method: Record a failed job through the real `go` flow with the fake scripted reader, producer and introspection (existing helper `reject(&model, &athena, text, None, true)` in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs:115). Call `athena.retry_by_hand(&job, false, &Lines::default())` once and read back the Proposed retry. Count `request_jobs()` and take `fx.head()`. Call `retry_by_hand` again and assert Err. The error must contain the first retry's id, its state, and 'Nothing was queued'. `fx.head()` and the job count must be unchanged. A second case uses `ask_by_hand("try again on <job>", false)` and `queue_by_hand`, and asserts both are refused with the same id. A third case uses the real binary: run `athena retry <job>` through `Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena"))` with ATHENA_STATE_DIR set, as `athena_bin` does in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs:292. It must exit non-zero with the id on stderr and leave HEAD unchanged. The refusal happens before any model call, so the binary needs no script.
demonstrations.observes: The refusal text names the existing retry id. HEAD, the record set and the job count are identical before and after. The binary exits non-zero.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the guard the second `retry_by_hand` queues a third job and returns Ok, so the unwrap_err, the unchanged HEAD and the unchanged job count assertions fail. Without naming the id, the `error.contains(first_retry_id)` assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Athena::retry_by_hand`, `ask_by_hand`, `queue_by_hand` (step 3) and the `athena retry` binary (step 4). Fixtures: `Fixture`, `Scenario`, `Model` and `reject` in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs and common/mod.rs, which exist. The scripted fake agent is injected through `fx.athena(model.script(scenario.script()))` (retry.rs:103-110, exists). The binary helper is copied from introspection.rs:292 into retry.rs (step 6).

demonstrations.method: Run `reject(&model, &athena, "remove the readme", None, false)`. Then, as `interrupted()` does (retry.rs:499-505), `git reset --hard HEAD~1` through `fx.git.run` until Records show no introspection for the job while its state is still Closed(Rejected). That is a rejected job whose review has not been written. Assert `failure_review_pending` is true. Call `retry_by_hand(&job, false)` and assert Err. The error must contain 'failure review' and 'pending'. HEAD and the job count must be unchanged. Then run the review (queue a scripted reply, call `athena.introspect_job`) and assert `retry_by_hand` now succeeds. A second case commits a Failed introspection whose failure text contains the kill-switch text and shows the job is still pending. A third case commits one with another failure and shows it is not.
demonstrations.observes: Refused with 'failure review ... pending' and nothing queued while no review record exists; allowed after the review record is committed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the pending check the hand retry succeeds and queues a job, so the assert-Err fails. Without the 'pending' message the `contains("pending")` assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::retry_by_hand` (step 3) and `failure_review_pending` (step 2). The state is built by the real `go` flow, with the fixture's `fx.git` used to drop the review commit (exists, as `interrupted()` does it).

demonstrations.method: With a rejected job whose introspection is Recorded and no retry: call `retry_by_hand(&job, false)` and `athena.retry(&job)` on a second identical fixture. Both give Ok with the same (proposal.reading.is_some(), seeded) pair and request text 'try again on <job>'. Also check that a retry that was dropped with `athena.close(&first, ...)`, one that ended Failed, and a Declined one do not block (`a_dropped_retry_does_not_block_a_new_retry`, retry.rs:1217, is the model). Run the whole file: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test retry`. Tests that use `athena.retry` and `athena.ask` directly must all still pass, including `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice` (retry.rs:1282), which now carries a comment saying it exercises the automatic path.
demonstrations.observes: Hand retry is queued exactly as `retry` does; the existing retry.rs tests are green.
demonstrations.fails_without: A guard that refused too widely (for example any failed job, or counting ended retries) makes the Ok assertion fail. `--force` on a job with nothing blocking must also not write an intervention; without that rule the 'no intervention' assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `retry_by_hand` and the unchanged `retry`. Fixtures exist in retry.rs.

demonstrations.method: Queue one hand retry. Call `retry_by_hand(&job, true)` and assert Ok with a second, different job. Load Records and assert exactly one new `Intervention` with category OverrodeDecision, source Observed, job == the failed job, and text naming the first retry id. Assert both retry jobs are Proposed and the new request text is 'try again on <job>'. Repeat for the pending-review case (force past a pending review). Assert `--force` with nothing blocking writes no intervention. A binary test asserts `athena retry --help` and `athena ask --help` list `--force`. Extend the existing option loop at retry.rs:1085-1091 and the clap test `retry_help_names_stale_jobs_the_merge_and_the_base_fallback` in main.rs:1471.
demonstrations.observes: A second retry job exists and one intervention record is committed; the status interventions_by_category count rises by one.

demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `retry_by_hand(job, true, ui)` (step 3) and the clap `--force` flag (step 4). The intervention is read back with `Records::load(&fx.git, &fx.head())` (exists).

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs build in-memory Records with the existing fixtures near status.rs:1512 and 3688. Case 1: a Closed(Failed) job with no introspection gives Some('failure review pending'). Case 2: the same job with a Queued retry gives a note containing the retry id. Case 3: an ended retry or a Recorded review gives None. A whole-path test in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs, `status_shows_failure_review_pending_and_the_queued_retry`, calls `athena.status()` and `athena.trace(&job)` after the real flow. It checks the `recent` JobLine's `failure_note` and the trace's, and the rendered `display::status` text, which is run by `cargo test -p athena-cli --test retry status_shows_failure_review`.
demonstrations.observes: `failure_note` is 'failure review pending' for the pending job and 'retry <id> queued' for the job with a queued retry. The rendered line shows it.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `failure_note` the field is None and both assertions fail. Without live-retry detection the queued-retry case shows nothing.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `Athena::status`, `Athena::trace` and `failure_note` (step 5). In-memory Records fixtures exist in status.rs tests; the git fixture exists in retry.rs.
